svg.title: i* Strategic Dependency (SD) model - Hospital Patient Administration System, initial release
svg.text: Dependum types and the dependency arrow (depender to dependee)
Assumptions, modelling choices and limitations - i* Strategic Dependency model
PURPOSE AND POSITION IN THE PROJECT
The SD and SR models were developed in Sprints 3 and 4, AFTER the initial release
had been built. They did not inform the original design. They are used here as
the evaluation lens for the alignment evaluation, and they are kept consistent
with each other: the SR is the same model with four actors opened up, not a
An arrow runs from the depender to the dependee with the typed dependum in the
middle. goal = a state of affairs the dependee must bring about; softgoal = a
quality to be satisfied, judged rather than verified; task = an activity the
dependee performs; resource = an entity the dependee produces or supplies. The
horizontal bar under an actor name marks a position or role rather than a
The hospital depends on the external scheduling service for available appointment
slots and on the funding organisation for an authorisation with an approved
amount and its limitations. Both are RESOURCE dependencies: the hospital needs
the thing, not the activity, and cannot produce it internally. This is the
socio-technical insight that the process models alone conceal, and it is the root
(1) The Clinical Nurse Specialist Administrative Support Team is subsumed into
the Clinical Nurse Specialist Team because the case study attributes no distinct
goal, task or resource to it. (2) The HPAS is not modelled as an actor: it is a
system, not an agent, and has no goals of its own. (3) External services appear
as dependees only, because the case study does not describe their internal
behaviour. (4) Urgency is modelled as a soft goal rather than a goal, because the
hospital has not agreed a complete set of urgency rules. (5) The model does not
quantify dependency strength or failure probability, so it identifies risks but
